finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Supplying a file path with a command injection payload.
finding.assumptions: The file path is derived directly from an untrusted input (argv[1]), and there is no validation or sanitization of this input before opening the file.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that std::ifstream::open on a pathname does not spawn a shell or execute commands; it merely opens a file descriptor. No OS command is invoked from the file path. Therefore no OS Command Injection path exists. Also, the code does not use system(), exec*, or similar APIs.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Supplying crafted input for 'word' or 'target' that leads to command injection.
finding.assumptions: The input for 'word' and 'target' is not validated or sanitized before being used in the 'wordLadder' function.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the entire code fragment for any invocation of OS-level command execution primitives such as system(), exec(), popen(), or any indirect call that could lead to shell command execution. The function wordLadder and its helpers perform only string comparisons, vector manipulations, and recursive traversal; no external command is constructed or executed. No call to system/exec/popen or similar appears in the provided code.
